title: Empirical integer-binning evaluation and automated fallback-ladder tuning for low-bit deployments
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Goal: Build an empirical evaluation harness that measures the impact of integer-binning (bit clipping) strategies for int8/int4 AWQ and GPTQ variants, derive per-model "fidelity corridors" and synthesize an automated fallback-ladder that tunes deploy-time thresholds. This ticket captures design of the harness, initial experiment matrix, decision logic for the fallback ladder, and integration points with the regression monitoring pipeline.

Background: Prior quantization regressions in staging showed occasional semantic regressions for a small but critical fraction of prompts after aggressive low-bit profiles. Existing evals focus on layerwise deltas and KL-style metrics; we need a production-oriented signal that maps to customer-visible degradation and can drive automated rollback/fallback decisions with low false positives.

Scope:
- Create an "integer-binning" perturbation runner that simulates common low-bit transforms (AWQ/GPTQ, per-channel clipping, and sign-bit heuristics) across a defined model matrix.
- Compute fidelity corridor statistics (per-cohort distribution of similarity + logprob shifts) and synthesize thresholds that balance sensitivity / false-positive rate.
- Implement a fallback-ladder policy (hosted and dedicated) that selects progressively safer deployment variants (e.g., int4->int8->fp16) when metric breaches occur.
- Wire outputs into the regression alerting system and Runtime rollout gates for automated or manual rollback triggers.

Non-goals: full reimplementation of eval suite; exhaustive layerwise per-model autotuning (follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Integer-binning harness runs across 6 reference models and captures per-prompt similarity and logprob deltas into the eval store.
2) Fidelity corridor computation produces an API that returns: baseline median, 90th percentile drop, and suggested soft/hard thresholds per cohort.
3) Fallback-ladder policy documented and implemented as a spec and prototype that can be consumed by rollout orchestration.
4) Integration test that triggers a synthetic regression in staging and exercises automated fallback to a safer variant.
5) Runbook and dashboard showing alert rates and false-positive estimate < 5% on historical traces.
test_plan:
- Generate a benchmark prompt set (2k prompts) stratified by length, domain (QA, summarization, instruction), and token-expansiveness.
- For each model in matrix, run: fp16 baseline, AWQ-int8, AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int8, GPTQ-int4 with and without per-channel clipping masks.
- Capture metrics: cosine/embedding similarity (reference embedder), token-level logprob delta, and top-k token overlap.
- Run 5 random seeds of weight perturbation to estimate variance.
- Validate threshold synthesis using holdout prompts (20% of set) and compute precision/recall for detecting customer-visible regressions (manual label sample).
- End-to-end smoke: simulate a deployment where AWQ-int4 breaches hard threshold and ensure fallback ladder moves to AWQ-int8 and then fp16 if needed.
metrics: Fidelity corridor metrics: median similarity delta (string), 90p similarity drop, median logprob delta, 95p logprob tail. Detection targets: true positive rate >= 90% for labeled regressions, false positive rate <= 5% on historical baselines. Operational: evaluation run time per model <= 2h for the 2k prompt set on CI sized runner; alert latency < 1m when integrated into regression monitor.
design_notes:
- Integer-binning: deterministic simulation algorithm that clips or re-buckets weight tensors into discrete bins to imitate AWQ/GPTQ transform without full re-quantization pipeline; faster for large sweep.
- Fidelity corridor: instead of a single scalar delta, compute a 2D corridor combining semantic similarity and logprob shift; thresholds operate on Manhattan distance inside normalized corridor.
- Fallback-ladder: policy is monotonic safety ordering (int4-AWQ -> int8-AWQ -> int8-GPTQ -> fp16) with configurable backoff durations. Ladder decisions should be reversible on fresh positive signal.
- Risk: some models show large variance by prompt length; per-cohort thresholds required. Avoid global thresholds that over-trigger.
- Trade-off: we bias thresholds towards low false positives to avoid needless rollbacks; manual override flag implemented for canary experiments.
implementation_steps:
1) Build integer-binning runner (python, eval-harness module) and add CLI + lightweight nD job manifest.
2) Add fidelity corridor calculator and store outputs in eval-store (schema v2).
3) Author fallback-ladder spec and prototype in rollout-orchestrator repo (PR).
4) Add monitoring dashboard and alert rule in Grafana + PagerDuty playbook for manual escalations.
5) Run full sweep and review results with PM/Applied-ML and Reliability.
Links: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QUANT/Integer-Binning-Harness, Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-orchestrator/pull/412
